title: Weight-Space Programming of Policies and Their Verification via Model Checking
why_wsp: An LLM writes all weights of a small ReLU policy network as numbers from a PRISM MDP and PCTL property, then edits them using dataset and Storm model-checking feedback, with no gradient descent.
domain: sequential decision-making / RL policies in PRISM MDPs (Frozen Lake, Transporter, Stock Market)
target: feed-forward ReLU policy networks, 1x16 (Frozen Lake) or 2x32 hidden layers (others); parameter count not stated
interface: direct values (LLM outputs all weights as JSON numbers plus notes and self-check states)
loop: closed-loop with feedback (self-check retries, up to 5 dataset-repair rounds, up to 5 model-checking rounds)
self_editing: no; LLM writes and edits a separate policy network (it edits its own previously written design via notes)
fraction_or_count_of_weights_changed: all weights written from scratch: 'an LLM writes all weights of a policy network'

headline_results.claim: All 18 RQ1 runs reach optimal probability after creation step alone
headline_results.quote: All 18 runs reach the optimal probability, all of them already after Step 1

headline_results.claim: Kimi created networks pick optimal action in 98.9% of states; 100% after dataset repair
headline_results.quote: The created networks of Kimi-K3.1-Pro select an optimal action in 98.9% of the states on average; after Step 2, they do so in all states in all nine runs.

headline_results.claim: DeepSeek transporter accuracy only 59.5% yet optimal probability
headline_results.quote: only 59.5% on the transporter, where two of its three networks select an optimal action in only 39% of the states.

headline_results.claim: Generalization 2->3 jobs in 4 of 6 networks; failing ones get probability 0
headline_results.quote: For each LLM, two of the three networks also reach the optimal probability with three jobs, although the LLM never saw the three-job model

headline_results.claim: Fuel-reserve until-requirement satisfied in 6/6 runs; dataset repair broke it once and model-checking repair fixed it
headline_results.quote: Step 2 then raises the accuracy from 37.9% to 98.4%, but the most accurate network satisfies the requirement with probability 0. A single model-checking repair restores it

headline_results.claim: Most common error is wrong matrix shape
headline_results.quote: The most common error is a wrong network shape, in 32 of the 67 answers of DeepSeek-V4-Pro (48%) and in 8 of the 28 answers of Kimi-K3.1-Pro (29%).

cost.claim: Mean LLM calls per run (All: DeepSeek 3.6, Kimi 2.1 in RQ1; RQ3: 11.7 vs 3.3)
cost.quote: DeepSeek-V4-Pro needs 11.7 calls per run on average, Kimi-K3.1-Pro 3.3.
Each run makes at most (1+E+R-1)·(r+1)=30 LLM calls
DeepSeek-V4-Pro sent 67 requests for its 12 runs, Kimi-K3.1-Pro 29

baselines_and_controls: Optimal probabilities and optimal-action datasets computed by Storm as reference; comparison between two LLMs and across pipeline steps. No RL-trained or random baselines.
runs_and_variance: 3 seeds per configuration (temperature 0, cloud nondeterminism): 'we repeat each experiment three times with the seeds 1, 2, and 3' (Sec 5.1); means reported, no variance/CIs; authors call numbers 'indicative rather than precise estimates'.
robustness_of_edits: Generalization test only (2-job networks checked on 3-job model without change: 4/6 optimal). No fine-tuning/quantization tests.
verification: formal: probabilistic model checking of induced DTMC against PCTL with Storm via COOL-MC; every returned policy verified (threshold = optimum minus 1e-4)
memorization_vs_reasoning: Authors flag contamination risk: 'we cannot rule out that the LLMs saw these models or related policies during training' (Sec 6). Self-check catches cases where weights do not encode LLM's own intended policy.
limitations_stated: Small environments/networks (max 16,496 states, 2x32 hidden); two LLMs, three seeds; repair step rarely exercised (23 of 24 created policies already satisfied property); LLMs lose count writing long matrices; no guarantee a satisfying network is found within R rounds; possible training-data contamination.
cites_or_builds_on: Takehi et al. 2026 'Sparks of weight-space programming' blog [2]
Zheng et al. 2026 arXiv:2611.04268 (WSP for image-restoration diffusion)
notes_for_survey: Couples WSP policy writing with formal probabilistic model checking so every returned policy has a computed (not estimated) satisfaction probability. Shows dataset accuracy is a poor proxy for property satisfaction. Proposes setting as a WSP benchmark with Storm ground truth.
